title: Non-blocking follow-ups from frontend-position-risk-columns review (PR #257)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #257 (frontend-position-risk-columns), recorded here so they aren't lost once the PR merges.

checklist.step: PositionsTable's new usePortfolioRisk() call never checks riskQuery.isError/isLoading, so a genuine GET /api/portfolio/risk failure (as opposed to a specific ticker simply being absent from the risk response, which is already handled and tested) silently renders '—' in the new Protective Stop/Profit Target columns — indistinguishable from 'no stop/target configured'. RiskPanel, driven by the exact same usePortfolioRisk() hook/queryKey and rendered on the same PortfolioPage, correctly shows a full ErrorState for this case instead. Add the same isError handling PositionsTable already has for deletePosition.isError (an ErrorState block above the table) for riskQuery.isError too.

HeldPositionBanner has the identical gap, but it's worse there: a GET /api/portfolio/risk failure while GET /api/portfolio still succeeds leaves the banner silently showing 'Current Stop: —' on the Stock Detail page with no error indication anywhere on that page (RiskPanel's error state is a different page, Portfolio, and per the finding above PositionsTable doesn't surface it either). Decide and record an explicit degrade behavior for this case (e.g. a small inline warning icon/tooltip on the affected field rather than the component returning as if the position has no stop, or continuing to render null/absent-but-documented) rather than silently treating a query failure the same as 'no data yet'.

Correct this task's decisions entry #4 (HeldPositionBanner's unconditional-rendering rationale), whose claim 'a genuine usePortfolio/usePortfolioRisk fetch failure here is already surfaced loudly by PositionsTable/RiskPanel on the Portfolio page itself' is factually inaccurate for PositionsTable (no isError handling exists there, per the first finding above) and inapplicable for HeldPositionBanner's own page (StockDetailPage, not PortfolioPage). Add a corrective decisions entry (per CLAUDE.md's decision-memory rule) once the above two items are resolved, rather than leaving the original claim uncorrected.

decisions.decision: PositionsTable now shows a common/ErrorState block for riskQuery.isError, positioned above (and stacked with) the existing deletePosition.isError block, rather than hiding the table or replacing its risk columns' '—' fallback with something else. HeldPositionBanner instead shows a small inline warning icon (MUI WarningAmberIcon) wrapped in a Tooltip carrying the backend's error.detail, on both the Current Stop and Profit Target fields specifically, rather than a page-level ErrorState block of its own.
decisions.rationale: PositionsTable already has the ErrorState-block-above-the-table pattern established for deletePosition.isError, and RiskPanel (same hook/queryKey) already uses a full ErrorState for this exact failure -- reusing that pattern keeps all three surfaces driven by usePortfolioRisk consistent, and the table's own other columns (ticker/quantity/cost basis/etc., all sourced from the already-successful GET /api/portfolio) remain fully usable underneath the banner, so hiding the whole table would throw away real, unaffected information. HeldPositionBanner is different: it is a small supplementary panel embedded within StockDetailPage (which has its own, unrelated useStockAnalysis loading/error handling for the rest of the page), not a page in its own right, so a second full ErrorState block competing for space felt disproportionate to a two-field failure -- an inline warning icon/tooltip (the same icon-plus-tooltip pattern common/IbkrStatusBadge already uses for a degraded connectivity state) scopes the failure indication to exactly the two fields it actually affects (Current Stop, Profit Target), leaving the unaffected Entry Price field (sourced from GET /api/portfolio, not /risk) rendering normally. The rejected alternative -- continuing to render '—' during a genuine fetch failure -- was rejected because it is factually misleading here specifically: '—' already has an established, different meaning on this exact field ('no stop/target configured', e.g. a ticker absent from a *successful* risk response), and collapsing a fetch failure into that same glyph tells the user something false (that their position has no stop) rather than merely incomplete.

decisions.decision: Corrective decisions entry (per CLAUDE.md's decision-memory rule and this task's own checklist item 3): frontend-position-risk-columns' decisions entry #4 claims 'a genuine usePortfolio/usePortfolioRisk fetch failure here is already surfaced loudly by PositionsTable/RiskPanel on the Portfolio page itself' as the rationale for HeldPositionBanner returning null/absent rather than its own error state. That claim was factually inaccurate on both halves at the time it was written: PositionsTable had no riskQuery.isError handling at all (confirmed by reading the pre-fix component -- only deletePosition.isError was checked), and even if it had, RiskPanel/PositionsTable render on PortfolioPage, a different route from StockDetailPage (where HeldPositionBanner actually renders) -- a user viewing a held ticker's Stock Detail page during a GET /api/portfolio/risk outage would see no error indication anywhere on the page they were actually looking at, regardless of what a different page does. This entry does not retract the rest of decision #4 (HeldPositionBanner's unconditional rendering independent of useStockAnalysis, and its null-return for the not-yet-loaded/not-held case) -- both remain correct and unchanged; only the fetch-failure-is-already-handled-elsewhere claim was wrong, and is superseded by this task's own decision above (HeldPositionBanner now handles riskQuery.isError explicitly, with its own inline indication, rather than relying on another page to do so).
decisions.rationale: CLAUDE.md's Autonomous pipeline section calls for exactly this: a corrective decisions entry rather than an in-place rewrite of the original task's decision text, since frontend-position-risk-columns.json has already merged and its decisions array is that task's own historical record -- adding a new, dated entry here (on the follow-up task the inaccuracy was actually filed against) keeps both the original claim and its correction visible and dated, rather than silently editing history.

decisions.decision: Fix for pr-reviewer's blocking PR #258 finding (both PositionsTable and RiskPanel independently calling usePortfolioRisk() and rendering their own full common/ErrorState on the same PortfolioPage, producing two identical stacked role="alert" blocks for one underlying GET /api/portfolio/risk failure): removed PositionsTable's own riskQuery.isError ErrorState block entirely, reverting it to the silent per-row '—' fallback it had before this task started (the same fallback riskByTicker already renders for a ticker simply absent from a *successful* risk response). RiskPanel's pre-existing ErrorState remains the sole page-level error surface for this shared query. Updated PositionsTable's doc comment and PositionsTable.test.tsx's coverage of this case accordingly (now asserts no alert renders and the table still shows '—'), and added a new PortfolioPage.test.tsx regression test asserting exactly one role="alert" appears when GET /api/portfolio/risk fails with both PositionsTable and RiskPanel mounted together -- the exact page-level composition PositionsTable.test.tsx's standalone rendering couldn't catch and that let this bug ship in PR #258 in the first place.
decisions.rationale: The reviewer's own suggested fix (degrade PositionsTable back to its pre-task silent behavior, since RiskPanel already owns a full ErrorState for the identical hook/queryKey on the same page) was chosen over the alternative of keeping PositionsTable's block but suppressing RiskPanel's, or hoisting a single shared error banner up to PortfolioPage itself: RiskPanel's ErrorState already existed before this task touched anything, is more prominent (it currently gates RiskPanel's entire body, matching this task's own checklist item 1 rationale for why PositionsTable needed *an* indication at all -- RiskPanel already fully qualifies), and reverting PositionsTable is the smaller, more surgical change that doesn't touch RiskPanel's own established behavior or PortfolioPage's composition. A page-level hoist (PortfolioPage owning one riskQuery.isError check and passing the result down) was considered and rejected as overkill for this fix: it would mean PortfolioPage taking on a data dependency of its two children instead of staying the thin composition Frontend.md §3 calls for, for a problem a one-line revert on the offending component already fully solves. This does not reopen checklist item 1 (marked done): that item's actual requirement -- a genuine riskQuery.isError not silently rendering as '—' with zero indication anywhere on the page -- is still met, just by RiskPanel's existing ErrorState rather than a second one on PositionsTable; the checklist item's own literal suggestion ('add the same isError handling... for riskQuery.isError too') was the specific approach the reviewer's screenshot proved wrong for this page composition, per this decision. Left the two non-blocking followups from PR #258's review (HeldPositionBanner's duplicate aria-label; DashboardPage's own possible instance of this same sibling-duplication shape) on frontend-position-risk-columns-followups-followups, unchanged -- neither is the blocking finding this fix addresses.

comments.summary: Blocking: PositionsTable and RiskPanel are both rendered on PortfolioPage and both independently call usePortfolioRisk(); with this PR, a genuine GET /api/portfolio/risk failure now renders two identical, stacked common/ErrorState blocks (same heading, same error.detail, both role="alert") on the same page -- confirmed with a real browser walkthrough. PositionsTable.test.tsx's new test only renders PositionsTable standalone, so it didn't catch the page-level duplication with RiskPanel. The PR's decisions entry frames the new block as 'mirroring RiskPanel's own ErrorState' without accounting for both being composed on the same page.

Non-blocking: HeldPositionBanner's two warning icons (Current Stop, Profit Target) share the identical aria-label "Risk data unavailable" with no field-specific accessible name -- confirmed via browser (two icons rendered, both labeled identically). A screen reader user can't distinguish which field failed without relying on surrounding visual/DOM context alone. HeldPositionBanner.test.tsx's new test even asserts toHaveLength(2) for this identical label, so the duplication was noticed but not treated as a gap. Filed as a followup.

Non-blocking, pre-existing (not touched by this PR's diff): DashboardPage composes RiskSummaryCard and SellFlaggedPositionsCard, which both independently call usePortfolioRisk() and both render their own ErrorState on isError -- the same sibling-duplication shape as the blocking finding above. Worth a follow-up spot-check for whether Dashboard has the identical duplicate-alert bug, and fixing all instances of this pattern consistently if so. Filed as a followup.

review.notes: Verified frontend vitest (763/763, coverage well above 90% gate), backend pytest (1144 passed, 99.95% coverage), backend ruff+mypy clean, frontend eslint+tsc clean, check_profit_target_wording.py clean. Ran the persisted e2e suite (make e2e): 21/21 Playwright specs passing. No Playwright MCP tool was available in this session, so drove a headless Chromium directly (via frontend's installed @playwright/test) against a manually-started fixture-mode backend + vite dev server, simulating a genuine GET /api/portfolio/risk 503 for a held AAPL position on both PortfolioPage and StockDetailPage -- this found the blocking duplicate-ErrorState bug above; non-error paths on both pages render correctly with no regression. Cross-checked the corrective decisions entry (#2) against the parent task's original decision #4: confirmed accurate -- PositionsTable genuinely had no riskQuery.isError handling before this PR, and PositionsTable/RiskPanel render on PortfolioPage while HeldPositionBanner renders on the separate StockDetailPage, so the correction's characterization holds.
